text:
maria: Heads-up: canary p99 latency jumped ~30% after the runtime merge landed yesterday (commit ab12c3e). Seen on canary-3 in us-west1. Not in prod yet but it's a rollout blocker.

ci-bot: build/6789 deployed to canary-3 at 2025-11-02T03:12Z — automated perf checks flagged p99 increase. Logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/runs/6789

jin: i'm on it. quick question — do we have a repro run for the perf job? which inputs?

maria: repro harness is perf/harness/serve-smallseq. We saw p50 stable, p99 up. Use the same seed set: seeds/edge-requests-v2.json. I can share a tar of logs.

ankit: initial flamegraph looked like kernel_selection::choose_kernel hotpath and kv_cache::evict_walk spiking. Could be the new selection heuristic (threshold tweak) causing more kernel swaps mid-request => cache churn.

sam: copying the repro steps here so folks can run locally:
```
# on a machine with same docker image as canary-3
git checkout ab12c3e~1  # baseline known-good
./tools/run_perf_harness.sh --workload serve-smallseq --seeds seeds/edge-requests-v2.json --out /tmp/baseline --runs 10
# then current tip
git checkout ab12c3e
./tools/run_perf_harness.sh --workload serve-smallseq --seeds seeds/edge-requests-v2.json --out /tmp/after --runs 10
# compare p99
python tools/compare_perf.py /tmp/baseline /tmp/after
```

alisha: note: the canary image has KERNEL_SELECTOR_MODE=auto and KV_EVICT_WINDOW=256 by default. try setting KERNEL_SELECTOR_MODE=fixed to force previous kernel to avoid selector logic and see if p99 drops.

maria: good call. if fixed mode restores perf that narrows it down. jin, can you bisect kernel-selector commits in that range? ab12c3e includes a few changes.

jin: plan: git bisect between ab12c3e~30 and ab12c3e. i'll run the harness for each commit but want to parallelize. proposing this pattern:
```
# bisect script (local)
git bisect start ab12c3e good-known-hash
# for each bisect step run minimal harness (3 runs) and fail if p99 > baseline * 1.15
#automate with: tools/git-bisect-perf.py --workload serve-smallseq --seeds seeds/edge-requests-v2.json --metric p99 --threshold 1.15
```

ankit: also capture perf counters and a small heap of KV metrics per run: KV_CACHE_HITS, KV_CACHE_EVICTS, KV_CACHE_SIZE, KERNEL_SWITCHES. Add these to comparison so we don't chase noise.

maria: i'll upload the canary trace and flamegraphs to shared folder: s3://redwood-debug/perf/2000001234/ — includes top-down and per-thread samples.

ops-bot: created incident PERF-2316 (status: triage) — assigning @maria and @jin.

sam: if bisect narrows to a small change, please don't merge any runtime changes to main. we should also pin canary to previous version until we have a plan.

jin: quick update — after 3 bisect steps I'm seeing the regression appear when a single commit touching kernel heuristics and kv window landed together. I'll try toggling the env flags to isolate which sub-change matters.

alisha: add this to the test matrix: run harness with KERNEL_SELECTOR_MODE=fixed and KV_EVICT_WINDOW=512 to see if larger window helps. if both mitigations reduce p99, we might do a short-term revert on the heuristic change and land a separate tuning PR.

maria: agreed. also want to run a long-run (50k requests) reproduce in staging because intermittent cache thrash might only show up at scale. I'll schedule that overnight.

jin: FYI i'm packaging a minimal bisect artifact (docker image + seed tar + script) so others can run locally without rebuilding. ETA 30m.

sam: thanks. once jin posts artifact, i'll kick off parallel bisect runners on a few builders to speed up. keep logs in the s3 path please.

maria: thanks all — leaving notes in the incident. next steps: jin runs automated bisect, ankit and alisha validate mitigations (fixed mode + larger window), sam coordinates canary pin if we need immediate rollback. ping here with results. :thumbsup:
